name: Felixé Minas Haus Tannheim
kurzbeschreibung: The Felixé Minas House in Tannheim: 300-year-old listed townhouse with original Baroque and Biedermeier living culture in the Tannheimer Tal.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Felixé Minas House is located in the picturesque village center of Tannheim in the Tyrolean Tannheimer Tal (Reutte district) at Höf 43, at an altitude of approximately 1,097 meters above sea level. Nestled in the high-altitude Alpine valley near the Bavarian border, this listed property, built around 1698, is one of Tyrol's most culturally significant and authentic bourgeois and farmhouses. As a fascinating cultural monument, the house offers a perfectly preserved insight into the prosperity, artistic sensibility, and daily life of an influential Tyrolean merchant and magistrate family over three centuries.

Route & Requirements

The building owes its name to the last private owner, Felix Rief, who was simply called Felixé Mina in the village after his father Felix ("Felixé") and his mother Mina. After his death, the intact building, including its complete historical inventory, passed into the possession of the municipality and a foundation. The stately central-corridor house combines the traditional log construction of the Außerfern region with grand stone architecture.

Visit & Arrival

The Felixé Minas House is open to visitors during the summer season from early June to mid-October, and during the winter season from late December to late March, on Thursdays and Fridays from 14:00 to 17:00. Special guided tours for groups of 8 or more are available year-round by telephone appointment. Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €5.00, seniors approx. €4.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €2.50, toddlers free; family ticket approx. €12.00. Holders of the Tannheimer Tal Summer Guest Ticket receive discounted admission. Arrival by car: Via the A7 motorway (exit Oy-Mittelberg) or via Reutte on the B199 (Tannheimer Straße) directly to Tannheim; parking is available at the community center or at the Tannheim cable cars. By public transport: Train to Sonthofen (D) or Reutte in Tirol station, from there regional valley buses (line 120) run directly to the Tannheim Kreisverkehr / Gemeindeamt stop.

Tips

The ground floor of the historic house is accessible via a few steps; the upper rooms are reached by a historic wooden staircase, which is not wheelchair accessible. Take your time for the explanations from the knowledgeable cultural guides, who tell lively anecdotes about village life in past centuries. Combine your visit with a walk to the nearby Vilsalpsee lake in the nature reserve of the same name, to experience the impressive nature of the region and gain unforgettable impressions for your entire holiday in Tyrol.
oeffnungszeiten: Seasonally Thu & Fri 14:00–17:00 (groups by arrangement year-round)
